title: Shapes with clip-path
summary: circle(), polygon() and inset() cut a box into a shape; everything outside the shape is hidden.
explanation: clip-path hides every part of the element outside a shape. circle(closest-side) gives a circle that touches the nearest edges, inset(…) a rectangle with optional rounded corners, and polygon() takes a list of x y points, so a triangle is three points and a hexagon six.
Unlike border-radius, it can make any straight-edged shape. The slanted hero edge at the bottom is a polygon whose last two points are at different heights.
Clipping cuts off borders and shadows too, because they are outside the shape. Hover still only reacts inside the visible part.
tryThis: Change the triangle's first point from 50% 0 to 0 0: it becomes a right-angled triangle.
Change the hero's 85% to 60%: the slant gets steeper.
Add box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px black to .hex: the shadow is clipped away.
Change .notch's clip-path to inset(10px round 12px): a smaller rounded square.
